title: Nvidia Stock Bounces 2% as Chip Rebound Follows Brutal Friday Rout, Even as Melius Slashes Price Target - International Business Times Australia
body: Nvidia shares rose nearly 2% in early trading Monday as chip stocks rebounded from a punishing sell-off at the end of last week, though an analyst price-target cut highlighted lingering worries about artificial intelligence spending. Nvidia stock gained $3.68, or 1.80%, to $208.32 shortly after the open. The shares had closed at $204.64 on Friday. The gains follow a steep decline on Friday, when Nvidia fell 4.22%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged more than 7% that day, and the Nasdaq fell nearly 3%. The sell-off was driven by concerns that massive spending on AI infrastructure by technology giants may not generate adequate returns. Intel shares tumbled 28.58% after the chipmaker issued a weak outlook, one of the worst single-day drops in its history. Investors also reacted to Alphabet's historic share price slump last week and to Amazon's much larger-than-expected capital spending. On Monday, chipmakers including Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, Micron and Broadcom traded higher as investors looked to buy the dip. Intel remained under pressure. Nvidia had a difficult October. The stock fell about 10% during the month after hitting a record close of $239.24 early in October. Its 52-week range runs from $164.27 to $243.37. The stock's 50-day moving average is about $222, while its 200-day average is about $204, a key technical level that the shares tested on Friday. Despite the recent pullback, Nvidia has risen about 15% this year, slightly ahead of the S&P 500. Melius Research lowered its price target on Nvidia to $315 from $420 on Monday, but kept its buy rating. Analysts remain overwhelmingly positive on the stock. Of the analysts covering Nvidia, 54 rate it a buy or strong buy and one rates it a hold, according to MarketBeat. The average price target is about $321, well above the current price. Not everyone believes the sell-off is over. Veteran trader Tom Sosnoff said the decline in chip stocks may be "just the beginning," arguing that Nvidia, AMD and Micron would need to fall 25% to 35% before they look oversold. Some technical analysts have also described Nvidia's chart as damaged and warned that a break below key support levels could lead to further weakness. Nvidia's fortunes are closely tied to spending on AI data centers by companies such as Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta. Those companies have continued to raise their capital spending plans. Amazon now expects to spend about $220 billion this year and said spending would rise significantly in 2027, while Alphabet expects to increase spending significantly next year. That spending supports demand for Nvidia's chips, but investors are increasingly questioning whether the investments will pay off, putting pressure on AI-related stocks. Nvidia is expected to report its quarterly results later this month, a key event for the AI trade. Investors will look for signs that demand for its chips remains strong despite concerns about customer spending. Elsewhere in the chip sector, Marvell Technology agreed to buy Lumentum, according to market reports Monday. Nvidia's near-term direction is likely to depend on broader sentiment toward AI spending and the results of its upcoming earnings report. Monday's bounce offered relief, but analysts say volatility is likely to continue.

TradingKey - Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) will report its third-quarter 2026 financial results after the U.S. market close on November 3, Eastern Time, and host an earnings conference call at 17:00 on the same day. Ahead of the earnings report, AMD's stock experienced a sharp correction, dropping 10.88% on October 30 to close at $504.80. Intel ( INTC ) issued a weak outlook, which, combined with the market's reassessment of returns on AI infrastructure investments, collectively weighed on risk appetite across the semiconductor sector. Wall Street expects AMD's third-quarter revenue to reach approximately $13.09 billion, up 41.6% year-over-year. Adjusted earnings per share are projected to reach $1.95, an increase of about 62% from $1.20 in the same period last year. The company previously provided revenue guidance of $12.7 billion to $13.3 billion, with an adjusted gross margin target of approximately 56%. AMD's current decline was first dragged down by Intel's weak guidance. Slowing PC demand, rising memory chip costs, and increasingly cautious enterprise IT budgets have raised market concerns that the semiconductor industry's recovery could become bifurcated. AMD also operates in the PC market through its Ryzen processors and therefore cannot completely avoid industry pressure. In the second quarter, the company's Client segment revenue reached $3.06 billion, up 23% year-over-year, but changes in the product mix led to a decline in average selling prices. If PC shipments remain under pressure in the third quarter, revenue and profit growth in the Client segment may still slow down even if AMD manages to expand its market share. However, the business structures of Intel and AMD are not entirely identical. Intel still needs to contend with the weakness in its traditional PC business as well as cost and capacity pressures from its in-house manufacturing operations, whereas AMD's growth focus in recent years has visibly shifted toward data centers. Demand for server CPUs and AI accelerators provides AMD with growth drivers distinct from the traditional PC market. In the second quarter, AMD's Data Center revenue reached $6.7 billion, up 107% year-over-year, accounting for approximately 58% of the company's total revenue; operating profit for the segment rose to $2.1 billion. Demand for EPYC server processors and Instinct AI accelerators was the primary driver of performance expansion. The third-quarter earnings report will further test whether this growth is sustainable. title: Ed Yardeni Sees AI Chip Rebound, Year-End Stock Rally — Warns Of Midterm Election, Iran War Risks - TradingView
body: Yardeni Research President Ed Yardeni said Monday that the recent artificial intelligence (AI) sell-off was not a full-blown rout but was “taking some air out of the AI bubble,” which he sees as a positive development. In an interview with CNBC-TV18, the strategist said he expects semiconductor stocks to rebound, adding that AI is a real technology that will become profitable, although identifying which technology companies will benefit most remains difficult. Yardeni also expects a year-end rally in U.S. equities but warned that midterm elections and geopolitical uncertainty could create further buying opportunities. Yardeni said the recent pullback has reduced valuations even as analysts continue raising earnings expectations for AI-related companies. The market veteran noted that semiconductor stocks trade at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of about 13.5, below the S&P 500's 18.5, adding that cloud revenue growth and substantial order backlogs support his outlook. In a research note, he said that analysts expect semiconductor industry earnings to grow 114.3% in 2026 and 77.9% in 2027. The note also showed that Microsoft ( MSFT ), Oracle ( ORCL ), Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) have combined remaining performance obligations of $2.5 trillion. Yardeni Research identified funding and delivering AI infrastructure as the key challenge to monetizing those commitments. The firm also said memory makers were sold out into 2029, giving them pricing power amid strong AI demand. Yardeni’s comments come after Friday's sell-off saw Intel (INTC) stock plunge 28.6%, SanDisk (SNDK) fall 13.5%, and AMD drop 10.9%. However, the analyst said investors were shifting from AI stocks into health care, financials and industrials rather than leaving U.S. equities. Turning to Tuesday's midterm elections, Yardeni warned that the U.S. stock market could face further volatility amid the possibility of renewed escalation in the war involving Iran. He said his firm had advised caution since September 15 and suggested investors consider holding back cash for potential buying opportunities following the elections or any further escalation. Yardeni also warned that greater political division after the elections could make future debt and government shutdown negotiations more difficult, potentially creating risks heading into 2027. Despite those concerns, he expects a year-end rally in U.S. stocks, typically referred to as a ‘Santa rally’, between Thanksgiving and the end of December. U.S. stock futures rose early Monday after a losing week on Wall Street, as investors looked ahead to earnings, jobs data and the midterm elections. S&P 500 futures gained 0.5%, Nasdaq 100 futures climbed 0.80%, and Dow futures advanced 271 points, or 0.52%, following a week of selling in technology stocks amid concerns over artificial intelligence spending. Sentiment toward the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq 100, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) remained ‘bearish’. title: Nvidia Isn’t the Only AI Winner. Qualcomm May Be the Next Stock to Watch - 24/7 Wall St.
body: Qualcomm is quietly lining up data center wins with the world's biggest hyperscalers, and the revenue clock is about to start ticking. Whether it can offset mounting handset headwinds before Wall Street loses patience is the real question. Qualcomm ( NASDAQ:QCOM | QCOM Price Prediction ) is trading at $181.51. The 24/7 Wall St. price target for Qualcomm is $225.91 over the next 12 months, indicating 24.46% upside. This wins the stock a buy rating with high confidence from the model. Most AI money is concentrated in GPU leaders, but Qualcomm is about to start booking data center revenue. Management says two custom silicon wins with global-scale hyperscalers should start generating revenue in the December quarter, and wafer production for both is already underway. The data center targets are $5 billion in fiscal 2027 and $15 billion in fiscal 2029. That is a real AI growth story attached to a stock that pays a 1.93% dividend (we featured seven other suppliers powering the AI data-center expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report here ). Over the past week the stock gained 3.3%. That followed a 10.13% slide over the past month. Shares are up 7.79% year to date and sit inside a 52-week range of $120.88 to $257.56. In fiscal Q3, revenue came in at $9.95B, ahead of the $9.67B consensus. Non-GAAP EPS of $2.21 came in just short of the $2.22 estimate, which ended a six-quarter beat run. Handsets fell 20% while automotive rose 61%. Recent headlines have been positive . Qualcomm announced a trial verdict win on October 13, declared its quarterly dividend and scheduled its fiscal Q4 report. Guidance for that quarter calls for revenue of $9.70B to $10.50B and non-GAAP EPS of $2.05 to $2.25. Management expects non-handset revenue growth to speed up from 24% in fiscal 2026 to more than 60% in fiscal 2027, on the way to $40B by fiscal 2029. Annualized automotive revenue leaving fiscal 2026 is now expected to reach about $7 billion, and BMW has named Qualcomm its lead compute silicon provider for ADAS and digital cockpits. The first high-bandwidth compute accelerator is due in mid-2027. If those targets arrive on schedule, our bull scenario reaches $243.13. Qualcomm expects its share of upcoming iPhones to be materially lower than 20%. It also sees Android revenue down 20% in fiscal 2027, an EPS drag of more than $1.50. Fiscal Q3 operating income fell 41.1%. Spending tied to the Alphawave and Modular deals raised expenses, and management plans double digit price increases to bring gross margins back to their historical range. Only 11 analysts have a bullish rating on the stock, while 23 rate it a hold . Even so, our bear case still lands at $190.77. Broadcom is the closest match because it already leads in custom hyperscaler accelerators, the market Qualcomm is entering. Broadcom’s AI semiconductor revenue rose 221% to $16.70 billion, yet the stock trades at a lower forward multiple than Qualcomm. Nvidia is the benchmark for AI valuation. Its data center revenue rose 117% to $89.023 billion. On forward earnings, Qualcomm trades at a higher multiple than either peer. Its edge is income and diversification. That makes the 24/7 Wall St. price target look reasonable. The 24/7 Wall St. price target of $225.91 comes with a buy rating and 90% confidence. The swing factor is whether hyperscaler revenue shows up in the December quarter. I’d grow more positive if the fiscal Q4 report confirms that growth and gross margins stabilize. I’d turn more cautious if handset drops deepen beyond guidance. On balance, I think the upside outweighs the risk. The projections rest on Qualcomm staying on track toward its fiscal 2029 targets. The biggest swing factors are execution in the data center and how quickly handset demand recovers.
